summary: Daily sales team meeting for June 2026, run by Chris Klevan with closers Richard Claessen and Ben Byrne and setter Kim Forbes-Sobers. Opens with wins, then projections — nine sets, 75% show rate — and individual pipeline updates. Kim reports the core setting problem is lead quality: FDQs, and prospects who have already seen Primal University and found $200 a month too expensive. Chris confirms paid ads are being switched on, a new VSL is being written with help from Cole Gordon's ads lead, and states a deliberate shift in target avatar away from good-to-great prospects toward people whose health is their only problem, former athletes, people with injuries, and people who have had a recent life event. The remainder is coaching: a discovery role-play with Ben as a 41-year-old prospect, a second role-play with Richard as prospect covering goal-expansion and trust objections, and technique feedback on staying neutral in discovery and not asking prospects why they don't just return to their old routine.
notable: Explicit instruction to move the target avatar AWAY from the stated ICP: 'we want to get less of like the good to great people and more people that like, the only thing they're really struggling with is their health, sort of people, like they've got business taken care of, or people that, you were former athletes, like, you know, our actual like avatar, people that have like actual kind of like somewhat injuries, there's had like a recent life event that caused them to be more intent to want to make a change, and actually have the money.' The stated ICP in data/icp.json says the opposite — 'they're kind of wanting to go from good to great'.

Confirms Primal University pricing from the setter side: prospects 'had seen the primary university and the 200 bucks a month was too expensive'. This establishes $200/month (or $2,000/year) as the real price of the downsell product, which matters for grading how it was quoted on live calls in this batch.

Richard describes a prospect he ran that day: 'he had 327, but he was, like, a little bit ago, he was 340' and 'he was like, never really worked out. Last time was 20 years ago' — a ~327 lb prospect he wanted to close, well outside the stated ICP exclusion.
Ben's pipeline includes a prospect being worked while recovering from surgery: 'Jorge, he's like still, you know, recovering from a surgery.'
Chris's coaching philosophy on not accepting a prospect's answer, up to and including ending the call, and the 'Shiva energy' framing for directness.
Repeated 1,200-client social-proof claim, used inside the role-play as the trust asset: 'we've worked with 1,200 clients and we've lost way more than that for a lot of clients.'

Ben was taking sales calls from an office he described as trespassing: 'I'm kind of just trespassing, but working on that problem-solving muscle.' Chris's concern was operational — 'If you blow a sale because of this, not good.'

As with the 1-1, two role-plays here contain full price presentations in prospect voice ('$6,000 is a dude kettlebell', 'What was the 6K?') and will read as sales content to anything classifying by transcript body rather than by file.
